stem: A delivery rider travels equal distances of 60 km each at speeds of 20 km/h, 30 km/h, and 60 km/h on three successive legs. Which mean of the three speeds correctly gives the overall average speed for the entire journey, and what is its value?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Using the arithmetic mean (20+30+60)/3 = 110/3 = 36.67 km/h; the AM applies when time intervals are equal, not distances.
The geometric mean (20*30*60)^(1/3) = 36000^(1/3) = 33.0 km/h is used for rates of growth, not for average speed over equal distances.
For equal distances the average speed is the harmonic mean: HM = 3 / (1/20 + 1/30 + 1/60) = 3 / (3/60 + 2/60 + 1/60) = 3 / (6/60) = 3 * 10 = 30 km/h.
There is no basis for a weighted mean here since all three distances are equal; a student might assign arbitrary weights and arrive at 35 km/h.

explanation: When a traveller covers EQUAL distances at different speeds, the appropriate average speed is the harmonic mean (HM). HM = n / sum(1/x_i) = 3 / (1/20 + 1/30 + 1/60). Common denominator 60: 3/60 + 2/60 + 1/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. HM = 3 / (1/10) = 30 km/h. Verification: total distance = 180 km, total time = 60/20 + 60/30 + 60/60 = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 hours, average speed = 180/6 = 30 km/h.

explanation_sections.punchline: Equal-distance speed problems require the harmonic mean - the AM overstates the true average speed because more time is spent at lower speeds.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: equal distances imply HM. Formula: HM = n / sum(1/x_i). n = 3, values = 20, 30, 60. Reciprocals: 1/20 = 3/60, 1/30 = 2/60, 1/60 = 1/60. Sum = 6/60 = 1/10. HM = 3 * 10 = 30. Verify by computing total time: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 h for 180 km giving 30 km/h.
explanation_sections.lesson: AM = equal time intervals; HM = equal distances; GM = equal multiplicative growth. The stem specifies which applies.
explanation_sections.timing: 50-60 seconds. Convert reciprocals to 60ths at once and sum, then invert and multiply by n.
